steps.instruction: Do something only when a test passes.
body: The test in brackets is true or false.
The braces hold what happens in each case.
=== checks the value and the type. !== is the opposite.
== also exists and converts before comparing, which produces surprises. Use ===.

steps.instruction: Compare the number 5 with the text "5" using ===.
steps.after: TypeScript stops you comparing a number with text, because the answer is always false and you probably did not mean it.

steps.instruction: Print "Old enough" when age is 16 or more, otherwise "Too young".

body: && needs both. || needs one. ! flips it.

steps.why: 8 is more than 5, and 8 % 2 is 0, so both sides of && are true. The first branch runs and the rest are skipped.
skills: read a chain of if and else if

body: It stops at the first test that passes.
Order matters. Put the narrowest test first.
steps.keypoint: else if chains stop at the first match.

steps.hint: Both conditions must hold. And comparison is always three equals.
steps.after: && for both, else for the fallback, === to compare.

steps.instruction: A value that could be one of two types.
body: string | number means either is allowed.
Inside the if, TypeScript knows it is a number, so * 2 is fine.
In the else it knows it is a string, so toUpperCase is fine.
steps.keypoint: typeof x === "number" tells TypeScript which one it is.

steps.instruction: Call toUpperCase on id without checking what it is first.
steps.after: id might be a number, and numbers have no toUpperCase. Check with typeof first and the error goes.

steps.instruction: Print "even" or "odd" for n, and "big" on a second line only when n is over 100.
steps.hint: Two separate ifs. The second one has no else.
steps.after: An if does not need an else when there is nothing to do otherwise.
